newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - Wall Street seen lower on U.S. GDP.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Wall Street seen lower on U.S. GDP.

text.p: NEW YORK - U.S. stocks, fresh from a record rise Tuesday, are expected to open lower on fears a surprisingly strong GDP number may encourage the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates.
The Commerce Department Wednesday reported that real Gross Domestic Product grew at an annual rate of 5.6 percent in the first quarter of 1997, a nine-year high.
ALAN ACKERMAN, MARKET STRATEGIST OF FAHNESTOCK & CO: "With this number, the Fed is ready now to feel that it can consider this (a rate rise) strongly."
He added, "It's likely to impact the very strong rally we had yesterday and take its toll on stocks that went up too quickly. ... We may have a blue-chip round of profit-taking."
LARRY WACHTEL, ANALYST AT PRUDENTIAL SECURITIES:
The numbers "were much stronger than expected. The bonds are weak and ... the bonds will lead the stocks."
PHIL ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER, VALUE LINE ASSET MANAGEMENT:
"We thought it would be a little stronger (than consensus) but we were blown away by this number."
"If yesterday's number created any wavering, this solidified the position that further tightening is in the cards. This confirms our view that the Fed is going to give us three tightenings."

"Unless there is some error (in the number) or some nuance we don't know about yet, it's going to lead to a reverse psychology for stocks, a mirror image of yesterday. ... A lot of equity money will be flowing into bonds."
"That (GDP) number will make people think that interest rates are probably going to rise at the next Fed meeting."
